5-Days UHV-II Refresher Workshop (24- 28 November 2025)

Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College (AKGEC), Ghaziabad, through its Value Education Cell , successfully organised an AICTE-approved, Self-Funded 5-Day Universal Human Values Refresher Workshop (UHV-II Refresher) from 24–28 November 2025 .
A total of 27 participants —26 from AKGEC and 1 from Arya College, Jaipur—enthusiastically took part in the workshop and successfully completed the program.
Objectives and Focus
The workshop was designed as a process-centric, outcome-based program with the following key objectives:

To enable participants to understand the reality of human being, family, society, and nature/existence through the process of self-exploration . To emphasize the importance of meaningful participation at all four levels of living— Self, Family, Society, and Nature —for a harmonious way of life. To provide a platform for reflection, dialogue, and experiential learning that connects Universal Human Values with both personal and professional contexts.

The sessions were structured to encourage deep inquiry, self-reflection, and collective exploration , ensuring that participants could internalize the principles of Universal Human Values in a practical and sustainable manner.
Resource Persons
The enriching and reflective sessions were facilitated by:
Dr. Gopal Babu , Head, Value Education Cell, AKGEC Dr. Manishi Mishra , Member, Value Education Cell

Both facilitators guided participants through a series of interactive discussions, experiential exercises, and reflective dialogues , creating an environment of openness and inquiry. Their expertise and commitment ensured that the workshop remained engaging and impactful throughout its duration.
Observer
The program was observed by Dr. Arvind Sharma , appointed by AICTE . His presence ensured the smooth conduct of the FDP in alignment with AICTE guidelines and added value to the overall proceedings.
Local Program Coordinator
Dr. Parul Verma and Mr. B N Pandey coordinated the entire program locally for the well-ordered conduct of the FDP.
Valedictory Session
The Valedictory Session was graced by Prof. Hemant Ahuja, Director, AKGEC .
Prof. Ahuja attentively listened to the participants’ feedback and reflections, which highlighted the transformative impact of the workshop.
He expressed his appreciation for their sincere engagement and active participation , acknowledging the depth of their involvement in the process of self-exploration.
In his address, Prof. Ahuja emphasized that harmony within naturally creates harmony outside , encouraging participants to remain in the continuous journey of self-exploration and value-based living.
His words served as a motivating reminder of the importance of integrating Universal Human Values into everyday life.
Outcomes and Commitments
The workshop concluded with a collective commitment from all participants to:
Carry forward the learnings of Universal Human Values into both personal and professional life .
Integrate these values into teaching practices, institutional culture, and social interactions.
Continue the process of self-exploration as a lifelong journey towards harmony and holistic development.
Participants expressed their resolve to embody these values, ensuring that education and professional practice remain rooted in human values and contribute to a more harmonious society.
Conclusion

The UHV-II Refresher Workshop at AKGEC was a resounding success , fulfilling its objectives of deepening participants’ understanding of Universal Human Values and reinforcing their commitment to value-based living.

By fostering reflection, dialogue, and experiential learning , the workshop not only enriched the participants but also strengthened AKGEC’s ongoing mission to integrate Universal Human Values into education and institutional life.
3-Day Universal Human Values Introductory FDP (01- 03 December 2025)

The Value Education Cell of Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College (AKGEC), Ghaziabad, successfully organized an AICTE-approved, Self-Funded 3-Day Faculty Development Program (FDP) on Universal Human Values (UHV Introductory) from 1–3 December 2025.

This FDP was designed to provide faculty members with a structured introduction to the foundational aspects of Universal Human Values (UHV), enabling them to integrate these principles into their teaching practices and personal lives.
Objectives and Focus
The program was process-centric and outcome-based , with the following key objectives:

To enable participants to initiate self-exploration for understanding the reality of human being, family, society, and nature/existence. To build clarity on living in harmony at all four levels of living— Self, Family, Society, and Nature . To encourage participants to connect Universal Human Values with both personal and professional life , ensuring holistic development. Sessions were designed to be interactive, reflective, and exploratory , fostering an environment of openness, dialogue, and inquiry.
Participation

A total of 26 faculty members from AKGEC actively engaged in the program. Their enthusiastic involvement reflected a genuine interest in exploring the UHV framework and its relevance to education and everyday living.
Facilitators
The sessions were facilitated by:
Dr. Parul Verma Mr. B. N. Pandey

Both facilitators guided participants through structured discussions, reflective exercises, and experiential learning activities , ensuring that the sessions remained engaging and impactful. Their facilitation style encouraged participants to deeply engage with the UHV framework and apply it meaningfully in their own contexts.
Coordination and Observation

The program was observed by Mr. Kaushal Gupta , appointed by AICTE . His presence ensured the smooth conduct of the FDP in alignment with AICTE guidelines and added value to the overall proceedings. Dr. Sumedha Sharma served as the Local Program Coordinator , ensuring effective organization and seamless execution of the FDP.
Valedictory Session
The Valedictory Session was graced by Prof. (Dr.) Gopal Babu, Head, Value Education Cell, AKGEC .

Prof. Babu listened to participants’ reflections and feedback, which highlighted the transformative impact of the sessions. He appreciated their sincere involvement and encouraged them to continue the journey of self-exploration . In his address, Prof. Babu emphasized that inner harmony naturally radiates outward , fostering harmony in family, society, and nature.
His words served as a guiding reminder of the importance of integrating Universal Human Values into both personal and professional spheres.
Outcomes and Commitments
The FDP concluded with a collective commitment from participants to:
Carry forward the learnings of Universal Human Values into teaching practices, institutional culture, and everyday living.
Continue the process of self-exploration as a lifelong journey towards harmony and holistic development.
Ensure that education remains rooted in human values , contributing to the creation of a more value-based and harmonious society.
Conclusion
The 3-Day UHV Introductory FDP at AKGEC was a successful and enriching initiative , fulfilling its objectives of introducing faculty members to the foundational aspects of Universal Human Values.

By fostering reflection, dialogue, and experiential learning , the program not only enriched the participants but also strengthened AKGEC’s ongoing mission to integrate Universal Human Values into education and institutional life.

Total Registration – 37 Total participants reported Day1 – 31 Participants continued FDP – 31 (3 colleges &2 national level participants) Completed with above 95% Attendance -31 Self-evaluation session recording done

The 5-Day UHV-II Refresher Workshop, approved by the All-India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), commenced from 28th July- 1st August 2025 at Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, Ghaziabad. This workshop serves both as a refresher for the Universal Human Values (UHV-II) Workshop and a preparatory platform for the upcoming UHV-III Workshop.

A total of 37 participants registered from the host institution and various external colleges, and 31 participants attended actively. The attendees primarily comprise faculty members who have previously undergone the UHV-I and UHV-II workshops and are now engaging in a deeper exploration of human values in education.
Workshop Objectives and Approach

A total of five sessions, including one small group discussion (GD) session, helped participants to explore and express themselves thoroughly. The whole workshop is designed to deepen participants’ understanding of human values through experiential learning, reflective dialogue, and participative exploration. It reinforces key concepts from UHV-II and lays a robust foundation for advanced learning in UHV-III.
The opening sessions guided participants to reflect on fundamental human aspirations: • Do we want to live? • Do we want to live with fulfilment? • Or do we want to live with continuous fulfilment?

Participants explored the meaning of continuous fulfilment based on natural acceptance, gradually transitioning toward observing their own internal state, rather than forming premature conclusions. The first step in this self-inquiry—observing the state of imagination and identifying the source of desire—was received with appreciation and enthusiasm.

Exploration of Happiness and Harmony A key theme explored during the workshop was happiness as harmony at all levels of human existence: • At the Individual level: Harmony between the self (conscious unit) and the body (material unit) • In the Family: Nine essential feelings for harmony, from trust to love, are seen as coexisting naturally • In Society: Four comprehensive goals (right understanding, prosperity, trust, and mutual fulfilment) are identified as coexisting harmoniously • In Nature/Existence: Four distinct orders of nature (material, plant, animal, and human) are understood to be in mutually fulfilling coexistence • In the larger Existence: All units of nature are in coexistence with the all-pervading space

This understanding reinforces that coexistence as the absolute truth is reflected at every level of human living. Recognizing this truth fosters a holistic and values-based worldview that integrates thought, behaviour, and interaction with the world.

Acknowledgements Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College sincerely thanks NCCIP and AICTE for their ongoing support and for providing a dedicated team of experienced facilitators. Their continued guidance plays a pivotal role in enabling educators to integrate Universal Human Values into the educational framework meaningfully. Outcomes As the workshop concluded on 1st August 2025, participants emerged with: • Enhanced clarity and conviction in values-based living • Greater alignment between realisation, thought, behaviour, and work • Improved capacity for self-reflection and inner harmony • Readiness for the upcoming UHV-III Workshop

FDP on Consciousness Engineering (17- 21 December 2024)
Dates: 17-21 December 2024 Place: ME Conference Hall, ME Block, AKGEC Total Registrations: 35 Total Participants: 26

A 5-day (17-21 December 2024) Consciousness Engineering workshop was conducted by Value Education (VE) Cell with the objective of the in-depth exploration of Feelings and Thoughts 'within' for the selected inclined faculty members of the institute. A total of 26 FMs inquisitively attended the workshop and participated in the exercise (including 7 Steps) of observing the Self (conscious unit) by Self and making an effort to understand the process of harmonious decision-making. This interactive workshop included four sessions per day and was facilitated by Dr Gopal Babu, Coordinator of VE Cell. The objective was to help the faculty members to see the self, the conscious entity; and also, the process of self-exploration.

The workshop was aimed to accomplish the following objectives: – Increase awareness levels – Develop the ability to counsel oneself – Improve the ability to sense our own and others' emotions – Enhance skills to handle reactions, both internal and external – Strengthen teamwork capabilities – Learn to take breaks when necessary – Improve listening skills – Gain wisdom in distinguishing between right and wrong

The workshop was divided into multiple interactive sessions, encouraging attendees to ask questions, provide reflections, and actively participate throughout discussions. Everyone was involved seeking clarifications and meaningful discussions.

The steps covered in the workshop were as follows: 1. Be aware– Observe your imagination at this moment, i.e., the desire (feeling), thought, expectation. No Reaction! [MFC: Observation/Conclusion] 2. Is the feeling that you have at this moment is naturally acceptable to you? [Feelings/Thoughts] 3. Are you in harmony, happy with the feeling that you have at this moment? 4. Who decided the feeling that you have at this moment? Did you decide it or someone else/situation outside decided it? 5. On what basis did you decide the feeling you have at this moment? Did you decide it on the basis of understanding or on the basis of any assumption? [is the feeling based on my assumption/his behaviour or right understanding/reality] 6. a) Which feelings are naturally acceptable to you? Feelings of relationship or opposition, harmony or disharmony, co-existence or struggle? b) Explore within to understand relationship, harmony, and co-existence in its completeness, in the context of whole nature and existence. 7. a) Ensure that the feeling that you have at this moment is in line with the feeling of Relationship, Harmony and Co-existence and not otherwise. On this basis, I will be in a state of harmony and happiness at this moment. b) when I am able to understand relationship, harmony and co-existence in its completeness, then, I will be able to decide my feelings and thoughts accordingly in a natural manner, and I will always be comfortable within, I will be in a state of harmony and happiness in continuity.

As part of an evaluation process, the participants were provided with a self-assessment form to gauge their comprehension levels. The one part of the form included four parameters: ‘awareness’, ‘ability to perceive one's own and other’s needs, ‘ability to manage internal and external reactions’, and ‘ability to provide self-counseling’ and the second part included every day key takeaways and a feedback form. Upon reviewing the completed forms, it was evident that many participants experienced improvement in these areas. Also, the participants in their sharing reflected that the workshop was productive in the purification of feelings and thoughts (SANSKARS) and felt sincere gratitude towards the authorities for providing such opportunities and environment in the institute only at desirable intervals.

An Experiential Exploration of Human Values (9-12 March 2023)

A four-day UHV activity-based workshop was organized by VE Cell, AKGEC in coordination with ISABS (Indian Society for Applied Behavioral Science) during 9–12 March 2023 (9 AM – 5 PM), in ME Conference Hall. The workshop was facilitated by Dr. Rashmi Saxena & Dr. Rachna Sharma(ISABS Professionals).Indian Society for Applied Behavioral Science (ISABS) is a national, nonprofit voluntary society of behavioral scientists engaged in applying their knowledge and skill to the well-being of persons, organizations, communities, and the society at large. The workshop was planned by Dr. Gopal Babu, Coordinator, VE Cell, AKGEC under.
The following faculty members (including Prof. V.K. Parashar, Head VE Cell, AKGEC) actively participated in this small group workshop-

FMs from the college | FMs from outside
Dr. Upasana Mishra, CSE | Mr. Bhanu Pratap Singh, AP, CSJMU Kanpur
Mr. Akhilesh Verma, CSE | Dr. Kumar Sambhav, UPID Noida, NCCIP Member
Mr. BN Pandey, CSE | Mr. Alok Pandey, KIET Ghaziabad
Dr. Parul Verma, ASH | Mr. NK Sharma, IMS Ghaziabad
Mr. RP Singh, ECE | Dr. Vanchna Singh, Self Employed
Dr. Jitendra Chaabra, ECE | Mr. Himanshu Kumar Rai (Guest Faculty, DU)
The following were the highlights of the workshop-
It was an unstructured workshop, where the experiential learning was in the Centre.
The workshop was specifically focused on observing feelings/emotions of the immediate moment (being aware and honest about – Here and Now).

Time, Territory and Task were cautiously cared for, disallowing any past reference or future assumptions ie avoiding Then or There), while interacting and dealing with participants and self-planned tasks.
The present was emphasized as the best-owned reality one can see.
Self-Image was recognized as a big challenge rather main culprit, responsible for the unawareness about feelings and behavioural ambiguities.
Availability of feelings, and acknowledging them, facilitates natural expression in behaviour. The same was exercised.
Expression has a CHOICE, may be verbal/nonverbal/pictorial/violent/nonviolent. The same was discussed and experienced.
The following were the main observations in the workshop-
The process connects with the first step of EXERCISE 1 of UHV, ie seeing the Self by the Self (without any reaction or evaluation).
Every moment of awareness about our being was been practiced formally.
The process is complementary to developing competence in observing feelings (emotions).
The existence (goal) is one similar reality, but the process/mechanism to know/understand the existence is variable.
Extracted Recommendations after the workshop were-
Integration of efficient steps (from various processes) may be evolved to suit the human desire of KNOWING/ UNDERSTANDING.
Participant’s periodic follow-up (online) is desirable to evaluate the gradual transformation.

Frequent such short crisp workshops may be planned, purposely for experiential validation (Steps of Exercise 1 and 2), for intense UHV explorers. This idea was shared with the honorable DG for his kind consideration.

FACULTY/STAFF DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS



5-DAYS UHV-II REFRESHER WORKSHOP (24- 28 NOVEMBER 2025)


Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College (AKGEC), Ghaziabad, through its Value Education Cell , successfully organised an AICTE-approved, Self-Funded 5-Day Universal Human Values Refresher Workshop (UHV-II Refresher) from 24–28 November 2025 .

A total of 27 participants —26 from AKGEC and 1 from Arya College, Jaipur—enthusiastically took part in the workshop and successfully completed the program.

Objectives and Focus

The workshop was designed as a process-centric, outcome-based program with the following key objectives:

To enable participants to understand the reality of human being, family, society, and nature/existence through the process of self-exploration . To emphasize the importance of meaningful participation at all four levels of living— Self, Family, Society, and Nature —for a harmonious way of life. To provide a platform for reflection, dialogue, and experiential learning that connects Universal Human Values with both personal and professional contexts.

The sessions were structured to encourage deep inquiry, self-reflection, and collective exploration , ensuring that participants could internalize the principles of Universal Human Values in a practical and sustainable manner.

Resource Persons

The enriching and reflective sessions were facilitated by:

Dr. Gopal Babu , Head, Value Education Cell, AKGEC Dr. Manishi Mishra , Member, Value Education Cell

Both facilitators guided participants through a series of interactive discussions, experiential exercises, and reflective dialogues , creating an environment of openness and inquiry. Their expertise and commitment ensured that the workshop remained engaging and impactful throughout its duration.

Observer

The program was observed by Dr. Arvind Sharma , appointed by AICTE . His presence ensured the smooth conduct of the FDP in alignment with AICTE guidelines and added value to the overall proceedings.

Local Program Coordinator

Dr. Parul Verma and Mr. B N Pandey coordinated the entire program locally for the well-ordered conduct of the FDP.

Valedictory Session

The Valedictory Session was graced by Prof. Hemant Ahuja, Director, AKGEC .

Prof. Ahuja attentively listened to the participants’ feedback and reflections, which highlighted the transformative impact of the workshop.

He expressed his appreciation for their sincere engagement and active participation , acknowledging the depth of their involvement in the process of self-exploration.

In his address, Prof. Ahuja emphasized that harmony within naturally creates harmony outside , encouraging participants to remain in the continuous journey of self-exploration and value-based living.

His words served as a motivating reminder of the importance of integrating Universal Human Values into everyday life.

Outcomes and Commitments

The workshop concluded with a collective commitment from all participants to:

Carry forward the learnings of Universal Human Values into both personal and professional life .

Integrate these values into teaching practices, institutional culture, and social interactions.

Continue the process of self-exploration as a lifelong journey towards harmony and holistic development.

Participants expressed their resolve to embody these values, ensuring that education and professional practice remain rooted in human values and contribute to a more harmonious society.

Conclusion

The UHV-II Refresher Workshop at AKGEC was a resounding success , fulfilling its objectives of deepening participants’ understanding of Universal Human Values and reinforcing their commitment to value-based living.

By fostering reflection, dialogue, and experiential learning , the workshop not only enriched the participants but also strengthened AKGEC’s ongoing mission to integrate Universal Human Values into education and institutional life.

The 5-Day UHV-II Refresher Workshop, approved by the All-India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), commenced from 28th July- 1st August 2025 at Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, Ghaziabad. This workshop serves both as a refresher for the Universal Human Values (UHV-II) Workshop and a preparatory platform for the upcoming UHV-III Workshop.

A total of 37 participants registered from the host institution and various external colleges, and 31 participants attended actively. The attendees primarily comprise faculty members who have previously undergone the UHV-I and UHV-II workshops and are now engaging in a deeper exploration of human values in education.

Workshop Objectives and Approach

A total of five sessions, including one small group discussion (GD) session, helped participants to explore and express themselves thoroughly. The whole workshop is designed to deepen participants’ understanding of human values through experiential learning, reflective dialogue, and participative exploration. It reinforces key concepts from UHV-II and lays a robust foundation for advanced learning in UHV-III.

The opening sessions guided participants to reflect on fundamental human aspirations: • Do we want to live? • Do we want to live with fulfilment? • Or do we want to live with continuous fulfilment?

Participants explored the meaning of continuous fulfilment based on natural acceptance, gradually transitioning toward observing their own internal state, rather than forming premature conclusions. The first step in this self-inquiry—observing the state of imagination and identifying the source of desire—was received with appreciation and enthusiasm.

Exploration of Happiness and Harmony A key theme explored during the workshop was happiness as harmony at all levels of human existence: • At the Individual level: Harmony between the self (conscious unit) and the body (material unit) • In the Family: Nine essential feelings for harmony, from trust to love, are seen as coexisting naturally • In Society: Four comprehensive goals (right understanding, prosperity, trust, and mutual fulfilment) are identified as coexisting harmoniously • In Nature/Existence: Four distinct orders of nature (material, plant, animal, and human) are understood to be in mutually fulfilling coexistence • In the larger Existence: All units of nature are in coexistence with the all-pervading space

This understanding reinforces that coexistence as the absolute truth is reflected at every level of human living. Recognizing this truth fosters a holistic and values-based worldview that integrates thought, behaviour, and interaction with the world.

Acknowledgements Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College sincerely thanks NCCIP and AICTE for their ongoing support and for providing a dedicated team of experienced facilitators. Their continued guidance plays a pivotal role in enabling educators to integrate Universal Human Values into the educational framework meaningfully. Outcomes As the workshop concluded on 1st August 2025, participants emerged with: • Enhanced clarity and conviction in values-based living • Greater alignment between realisation, thought, behaviour, and work • Improved capacity for self-reflection and inner harmony • Readiness for the upcoming UHV-III Workshop

FDP ON CONSCIOUSNESS ENGINEERING (17- 21 DECEMBER 2024)


Dates: 17-21 December 2024 Place: ME Conference Hall, ME Block, AKGEC Total Registrations: 35 Total Participants: 26

A 5-day (17-21 December 2024) Consciousness Engineering workshop was conducted by Value Education (VE) Cell with the objective of the in-depth exploration of Feelings and Thoughts 'within' for the selected inclined faculty members of the institute. A total of 26 FMs inquisitively attended the workshop and participated in the exercise (including 7 Steps) of observing the Self (conscious unit) by Self and making an effort to understand the process of harmonious decision-making. This interactive workshop included four sessions per day and was facilitated by Dr Gopal Babu, Coordinator of VE Cell. The objective was to help the faculty members to see the self, the conscious entity; and also, the process of self-exploration.

The workshop was aimed to accomplish the following objectives: – Increase awareness levels – Develop the ability to counsel oneself – Improve the ability to sense our own and others' emotions – Enhance skills to handle reactions, both internal and external – Strengthen teamwork capabilities – Learn to take breaks when necessary – Improve listening skills – Gain wisdom in distinguishing between right and wrong

The workshop was divided into multiple interactive sessions, encouraging attendees to ask questions, provide reflections, and actively participate throughout discussions. Everyone was involved seeking clarifications and meaningful discussions.

The steps covered in the workshop were as follows: 1. Be aware– Observe your imagination at this moment, i.e., the desire (feeling), thought, expectation. No Reaction! [MFC: Observation/Conclusion] 2. Is the feeling that you have at this moment is naturally acceptable to you? [Feelings/Thoughts] 3. Are you in harmony, happy with the feeling that you have at this moment? 4. Who decided the feeling that you have at this moment? Did you decide it or someone else/situation outside decided it? 5. On what basis did you decide the feeling you have at this moment? Did you decide it on the basis of understanding or on the basis of any assumption? [is the feeling based on my assumption/his behaviour or right understanding/reality] 6. a) Which feelings are naturally acceptable to you? Feelings of relationship or opposition, harmony or disharmony, co-existence or struggle? b) Explore within to understand relationship, harmony, and co-existence in its completeness, in the context of whole nature and existence. 7. a) Ensure that the feeling that you have at this moment is in line with the feeling of Relationship, Harmony and Co-existence and not otherwise. On this basis, I will be in a state of harmony and happiness at this moment. b) when I am able to understand relationship, harmony and co-existence in its completeness, then, I will be able to decide my feelings and thoughts accordingly in a natural manner, and I will always be comfortable within, I will be in a state of harmony and happiness in continuity.

As part of an evaluation process, the participants were provided with a self-assessment form to gauge their comprehension levels. The one part of the form included four parameters: ‘awareness’, ‘ability to perceive one's own and other’s needs, ‘ability to manage internal and external reactions’, and ‘ability to provide self-counseling’ and the second part included every day key takeaways and a feedback form. Upon reviewing the completed forms, it was evident that many participants experienced improvement in these areas. Also, the participants in their sharing reflected that the workshop was productive in the purification of feelings and thoughts (SANSKARS) and felt sincere gratitude towards the authorities for providing such opportunities and environment in the institute only at desirable intervals.

AN EXPERIENTIAL EXPLORATION OF HUMAN VALUES (9-12 MARCH 2023)


A four-day UHV activity-based workshop was organized by VE Cell, AKGEC in coordination with ISABS (Indian Society for Applied Behavioral Science) during 9–12 March 2023 (9 AM – 5 PM), in ME Conference Hall. The workshop was facilitated by Dr. Rashmi Saxena & Dr. Rachna Sharma(ISABS Professionals).Indian Society for Applied Behavioral Science (ISABS) is a national, nonprofit voluntary society of behavioral scientists engaged in applying their knowledge and skill to the well-being of persons, organizations, communities, and the society at large. The workshop was planned by Dr. Gopal Babu, Coordinator, VE Cell, AKGEC under.

The following faculty members (including Prof. V.K. Parashar, Head VE Cell, AKGEC) actively participated in this small group workshop-

FMs from the college | FMs from outside
Dr. Upasana Mishra, CSE | Mr. Bhanu Pratap Singh, AP, CSJMU Kanpur
Mr. Akhilesh Verma, CSE | Dr. Kumar Sambhav, UPID Noida, NCCIP Member

Dr. Parul Verma, ASH | Mr. NK Sharma, IMS Ghaziabad
Mr. RP Singh, ECE | Dr. Vanchna Singh, Self Employed
Dr. Jitendra Chaabra, ECE | Mr. Himanshu Kumar Rai (Guest Faculty, DU)

The following were the highlights of the workshop-

- It was an unstructured workshop, where the experiential learning was in the Centre.

- The workshop was specifically focused on observing feelings/emotions of the immediate moment (being aware and honest about – Here and Now).

- Time, Territory and Task were cautiously cared for, disallowing any past reference or future assumptions ie avoiding Then or There), while interacting and dealing with participants and self-planned tasks.

- The present was emphasized as the best-owned reality one can see.

- Self-Image was recognized as a big challenge rather main culprit, responsible for the unawareness about feelings and behavioural ambiguities.

- Availability of feelings, and acknowledging them, facilitates natural expression in behaviour. The same was exercised.

- Expression has a CHOICE, may be verbal/nonverbal/pictorial/violent/nonviolent. The same was discussed and experienced.

The following were the main observations in the workshop-

- The process connects with the first step of EXERCISE 1 of UHV, ie seeing the Self by the Self (without any reaction or evaluation).

- Every moment of awareness about our being was been practiced formally.

- The process is complementary to developing competence in observing feelings (emotions).

- The existence (goal) is one similar reality, but the process/mechanism to know/understand the existence is variable.

Extracted Recommendations after the workshop were-

- Integration of efficient steps (from various processes) may be evolved to suit the human desire of KNOWING/ UNDERSTANDING.

- Participant’s periodic follow-up (online) is desirable to evaluate the gradual transformation.

- Frequent such short crisp workshops may be planned, purposely for experiential validation (Steps of Exercise 1 and 2), for intense UHV explorers. This idea was shared with the honorable DG for his kind consideration.
